name: CyberAlchemy Lab Ontology Lifecycle
purpose: Coordinate the first event-sourced ontology vertical in the new CyberAlchemy-lab repository through the CAV2-D65 construction chain, while keeping product meaning, capability-local meaning, DomainSpec source, calculated runtime state, implementation evidence, and owner decisions in their separate authority lanes.
scope: the private clean-history CyberAlchemy-lab repository at ../CyberAlchemy-lab as the implementation target
the Ontology Lifecycle bounded context selected by CAL-ESOV-0003
one small Lab-native ontology witness before any legacy ontology migration
append-only typed semantic event streams per ontology node or relation with one graph-wide monotonic commit cursor
separate semantic and governance event streams joined by exact event identity, digest, and cursor

one CAV2-D65 prototype chain from definition prototypes and agent-facing ontology scaffolds through product, business-ontology, DomainSpec v2, compiled-graph, system-ontology, Rust implementation, frozen product candidate, current product tests, and product approval
exclusions: treating this Project record, repository path, generated graph, snapshot, projection, or validator output as semantic or execution authority
authoring DomainSpec source or Rust implementation before the required semantic predecessors and compiler profile are current
treating the prototype ConstructionBinding as a tested Lab product, product approval, or implementation authority
using calculated state, human views, indexes, or snapshots as a second canonical source
legacy ontology migration before the Lab-native witness is accepted
publication, release, deployment, external effects, or a stable-version claim
owner_routes: CyberAlchemy Lab Ontology Lifecycle Project owner

evidence_index.supports: The exact selected candidate fixes the target repository, Ontology Lifecycle context, per-subject streams, global cursor, complete resulting-state payloads, Rust reducer, calculated projections, separate governance streams, and Lab-first migration order.
evidence_index.claim_limit: The decision closes design choices only; it does not admit an ontology, authorize implementation, prove conformance, activate governance, or authorize migration.

evidence_index.supports: The exact readiness report identifies the D65 stage states, DomainSpec compiler gaps, and first semantic-predecessor task for the new repository target.
evidence_index.claim_limit: The readiness result is BLOCK; it is planning evidence and does not authorize DomainSpec authoring, Rust implementation, ConstructionBinding registration, migration, publication, or deployment.

challenge_route: Challenge the Project scope and target through the CyberAlchemy Lab Ontology Lifecycle Project owner, product meaning through the CyberAlchemy v2 product owner, DomainSpec construction claims through the DomainSpec v2 owner, runtime claims through the CyberAlchemy Lab ontology runtime owner, and source meaning through each exact source owner.
